result:
**Why it happened:** The JobRunr background job server was started while the application context was still being created. Jobs could therefore run before the context was ready. The commit message describes two failures on `jetty:run`. A job ran during the context refresh that follows module start, against the closed session factory of the context being replaced ("EntityManagerFactory is closed"). A module's job ran after the first, core-only refresh, before modules were loaded ("Task class ... not found"). (`openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/scheduler/jobrunr/JobRunrServerLifecycle.java:19-23`; commit `83411b2f8a52325e867fccc223a54d6a6f701400`)

**What core does now:** The server is started by a Spring `SmartLifecycle` (`JobRunrServerLifecycle`), so it runs only after its context has refreshed, and it stops before the context closes. A static flag, `deferStartUntilOpenmrsStarted()`, holds the start back. While the flag is set, `start()` returns without starting the server. `openmrsStarted()` clears the flag and starts the server if it isn't already running (`JobRunrServerLifecycle.java:43-64`).
- The webapp sets the flag at the top of `contextInitialized` (`openmrs-core/web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/Listener.java:207-209`).
- Modules are started, then `Context.getSchedulerService().onStartup()` runs. That calls `openmrsStarted()` (`Listener.java:355-372`; `JobRunrSchedulerService.java:97-99`).
- Contexts refreshed after startup start their server right away.
- Shutdown: the webapp never closes its context, so `JobRunrSchedulerService.onShutdown()` stops the server explicitly (`JobRunrSchedulerService.java:130-134`). The commit message says `Context.shutdown()` now calls it first. I did not read that method body.
- A test covers the deferred start (`openmrs-core/api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/scheduler/jobrunr/JobRunrSchedulerServiceTest.java:44-52`).

**Related but separate:** `ServiceContext.runOpenmrsServiceOnStartup` makes each service's `onStartup()` wait while a context refresh is in progress (`openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/context/ServiceContext.java:953-973`). It is a different gate and does not hold the job server.

**Change and ticket:** Commit `83411b2f8a52325e867fccc223a54d6a6f701400`, "TRUNK-6819: Start the JobRunr job server only once OpenMRS has started (#6654)", by dkayiwa. Ticket TRUNK-6819, PR #6654.

I did not modify any files. I used Falkon for everything, so this is not based on a local checkout.
